title: The ticket file is nothing but the build plan
intention: A ticket is three files with one job each: the plan (<id>-<slug>.json) holds only what a builder builds from; the state (<id>-<slug>.state.json) holds what the gates and doors read and write as the ticket moves (cursor, berths, chart claim, rehearsal pointer, fixme list, question ids, owner, class, model); the log (<id>-<slug>.log.jsonl) holds the trail, append-only as today.
why: Akien, 2026-10-29: "We talked about splitting up tickets into the ticket plan and the ticket log. the ticket becomes nothing but the build plan. that's what makes this work." Asked whether gate-read fields count as plan, he offered "it can include those fields or we break it into 3 parts: the metadata and state information, the plan, the history?" and ruled "three parts. record it and reshape the ticket." (open-c7809a745bf7). Measured that day: CairnCommons/tickets/_charter+why.json declares 56 plan_fields, trail and state keys among them; and the rehearsal hashes the whole ticket file, so every crossing or berth write stales a clean rehearsal although no step changed.
traces_to: Law 5 (the address carries what a mind needs now: the plan is the now, the log the trail); Law 1 (a builder re-reading the trail re-derives the settled); the spanning intention CairnCommons/intentions-not-beside-code/I-a-ticket-is-a-plan-and-a-log.md, whose plan carries 'only the fields the store charter's plan_fields declares'; c9897770efe6 (the rehearsal reads only the plan)
how: At cairn/tools/base/ticket_log.py (the ticket store's door): the store charter CairnCommons/tickets/_charter+why.json declares plan_fields (builder-read: id, title, intention, why, how, falsifier, traces_to, owning_intention, decisions, plus what the census shows a builder reads) and a new state_fields list (gate- and door-read, each with its reader named); every other key is log. One public read/write for the state file rides beside the plan's, through the artifact door. A first step measures, per field, its readers across cairn/ and skills/ and its fill count across CairnCommons/tickets/, written to CairnCommons/measurements/, and assigns each field to plan, state or log. One deterministic migration splits every ticket into the three files. Every reader of a state field (transitions, clearance, cast, question, the BUILDME lanes, the rehearsal pointer) reads it through the state door; the rehearsal hashes the plan file only. Supersedes the 10-10 placement of the cursor in the plan; there is still exactly one copy of where the work stands, now in the state file.
falsifier: Done when: every ticket under CairnCommons/tickets/ is a plan file holding only plan_fields, a state file holding only state_fields, and a log; each moved value stands in its new file; every crossing gate and door reads state from the state file and every proof under cairn/ that reads a moved field stays green; and a crossing that moves only the cursor leaves a clean rehearsal record's hash matching (it covers the plan only). Wrong intent if a builder or the rehearsal is stopped for want of something that now lives in the state file, i.e. the builder needed state, or a gate reds for want of something moved to the log.

decisions.text: D1 (the /sorted builder_check, reshaped 2026-10-29 by open-c7809a745bf7): a Haiku builder would ask: which fields go to plan, state, log (answered by the field census, the first build step); how a reader reads a state field (the state door beside ticket_log's plan read); whether the migration is one act (yes, one deterministic run through the artifact door, like 29569fca68a3); what a cast writes (cast_ticket writes all three files); what the rehearsal hashes (the plan file only). Each becomes a D-line at /chart once the census is taken.

D2: CairnCommons/tickets/_charter+why.json is rewritten through `cairn artifact write <path> --verb cast --why ... --from <file>`, and two keys change. A new key state_fields lists exactly the summary.state array of CairnCommons/measurements/2026-10-29-ticket-fields-plan-state-log.json (28 names, in that order). A new section "state" sits beside "log": {"file": "<hex-id>-<title-slug>.state.json beside the plan", "door": "cairn.tools.base.ticket_file (state_path, read_ticket, write_ticket)", "why": "Akien 2026-10-29, open-c7809a745bf7: 'three parts. record it and reshape the ticket.' The plan holds what a builder builds from; the state holds what a gate or door reads or writes as the ticket moves."}. plan_fields is NOT narrowed at this step (D11 narrows it in the same act as the migration), so no live ticket write is refused between the two.

D3: In cairn/tools/artifact/jurisdiction.json, under roots.CairnCommons.records, a new rule {"under": "tickets", "name": "*.state.json", "keys_from": "tickets/_charter+why.json#state_fields"} is inserted directly BEFORE the existing {"under": "tickets", "name": "*.json", ...#plan_fields} rule. Rules are matched first-match-wins (artifact.py locate and _refuse_undeclared_keys both take the first matching rule), so a state file is keyed by state_fields and a plan by plan_fields. Nothing else in the file changes.

D4: cairn/tools/base/ticket_log.py gains state_fields(plan) -> tuple[str, ...], read from the store charter exactly as plan_fields is (same _charter lookup). cairn/tools/base/ticket_file.py gains four functions: state_path(plan) -> Path, returning <dir>/<id>-<slug>.state.json beside <dir>/<id>-<slug>.json, raising ValueError for a name that does not end '.json' or already ends '.state.json'; plans(tickets_dir) -> list[Path], the sorted '*.json' files of the dir whose name does not start '_' and does not end '.state.json' ('.log.jsonl' never matches '*.json'); read_ticket(plan) -> dict, the plan's JSON updated with the state file's JSON when that file exists (a key in both takes the state file's value; only an unsplit plan carries one); and find_ticket(name, tickets_dir=None) keeps its current matching but takes an optional tickets dir (default the live one) and never returns a .state.json. write_ticket(path, doc, ensure_ascii, newline, *, why) keeps its signature and now splits doc: keys in state_fields are written to state_path(path) as json.dumps(..., indent=2, ensure_ascii=False) + newline, through door.write verb 'phase'; every other key is written to path in the measured shape, as today. The state file is written only when it carries at least one key.

D5: ticket_log.split(ticket, *, actor, why) sends each top-level key in state_fields to the state file (merged over any state file already there, written through write_ticket's state half) instead of the log, and leaves every other behaviour as it is: keys in neither plan_fields nor state_fields go to the log as kind 'field', phase_writes/rehearsal/retired decisions as before. It returns {'moved': {kind: count}} with kind 'state' counting keys moved to the state file. reconstruct(plan_doc, log, state=None) puts the state doc's keys back before replaying the log, so reconstruct(plan, log, state) equals the pre-split doc.

D6: transitions.cast_ticket(doc, *, actor, tickets_dir=None) accepts a key from plan_fields, state_fields, or a census log field (the census summary.log list, read from the charter key log_fields which D2 also adds with exactly that list); it writes plan keys to the plan and state keys to the state file through write_ticket, then each log-field key as one kind 'field' line through ticket_log.append_log; it still refuses (nothing written) a key in none of the three lists, naming it.

D7: Every ticket writer reads the ticket with ticket_file.read_ticket and writes it with ticket_file.write_ticket, so state keys land in the state file. The writers, by full repo path: cairn/tools/base/transitions.py (set_phase, its _write_ticket call), cairn/tools/question/question.py (where it writes questions onto a ticket), cairn/devices/trouble/trouble.py (where it writes node_class/schema_version/workflow_and_state onto a ticket), cairn/tools/chain/chain.py (its ticket write), cairn/tools/base/crossings.py (its ticket write), and cairn/machines/rehearsal/rehearsal.py (_write_ticket, which then writes only the plan half; the field it edits is decisions, a plan field). A writer that writes plan keys alone needs no change. D7 needs only D4 landed (it calls read_ticket/write_ticket); it does not wait on D8.

D8: Every non-proof site that lists the tickets dir itself is rewritten to ticket_file.plans(dir) (for a scan) or ticket_file.find_ticket(id, tickets_dir) (for one id), and every json load of a plan it found becomes ticket_file.read_ticket(path). The sites, measured 2026-10-29 by scratchpad globbers2.py, by full repo path: cairn/devices/cairn/machines/harbor_master/clearance.py, cairn/devices/cairn/machines/harbor_master/device.py, cairn/devices/tester/hollow.py, cairn/machines/build_inspector/inspector.py, cairn/machines/rehearsal/rehearsal.py, cairn/machines/rehearsal/probes/a_failed_run_is_counted.py, cairn/machines/skill_block/skill_block.py, cairn/tools/artifact/artifact.py, cairn/tools/base/cast.py, cairn/tools/base/cross.py, cairn/tools/base/crossings.py, cairn/tools/base/transitions.py, cairn/tools/base/watchme_spec.py, cairn/tools/base/ticket_file.py, cairn/tools/chain/chain.py, cairn/tools/chain/grammar.py, cairn/tools/operator_inbox/inbox.py, cairn/tools/proof_coverage/proof_coverage.py, cairn/tools/question/question.py, cairn/tools/ticket_inspector/inspector.py, cairn/tools/intentions_model_compiler/probes/present_tense_artifacts_carry_no_dated_appends.py, and the eight cairn/tools/base/probes/ files does_optional_mean_never_carried.py, no_component_reaches_proved_with_an_uncharted_build.py, no_ticket_carries_a_stored_chart_chain.py, no_ticket_carries_a_stored_crossing.py, the_casting_door_has_callers.py, the_ticket_write_door_has_callers.py, the_vocabulary_is_written_not_just_legal.py, unchartered_build_edits.py. In each file the site is any glob/rglob/iterdir/os.listdir call whose directory is the tickets dir; a glob over another dir (outline_checks, packets, design) is left alone. D8 needs only D4 landed.

D9: The proof cairn/tools/base/proofs/test_the_ticket_is_three_files.py is written red-first, before D2-D8, with PROVES = {'284798998ab0': {'all': 'test_the_ticket_is_three_files'}}: one composite tooth that runs the six and reds when any does (proof_coverage reads a declared tooth as one string). Teeth, each over a scratch tickets dir with a copied store charter: (1) the charter's plan_fields after D11 equal the census summary.plan, state_fields equal summary.state, log_fields equal summary.log, pairwise disjoint (read from the live charter and the live census); (2) the door writes a state file holding only state keys, refuses one holding a plan key, and refuses a plan write holding a state key; (3) write_ticket then read_ticket returns the doc it was given, with every state key in the state file and none in the plan; (4) plans() over a dir holding a plan, its .state.json, its .log.jsonl and _charter+why.json yields the plan alone; (5) split then reconstruct over a fixture v2 ticket returns the doc it split; (6) set_phase on a fixture ticket changes the state file and leaves the plan's bytes and rehearsal.design_sha of them unchanged. Run with --corpus, it instead checks every live plan under CairnCommons/tickets carries only plan_fields, every live state file only state_fields, and every plan has a state file; exit 0 only when all hold.

suite_parity.py already stands at cairn/tools/base/proofs/suite_parity.py, committed with the red-first proof (2162ff41) and written to exactly the contract D10 states; the builder does not write it again, it only runs --baseline before D2-D8 land and the comparison after. The baseline was taken before the build began and stands at CairnCommons/measurements/2026-10-29-suite-reds-before-the-ticket-split.json, so in build order this step is only the comparison after.

D11: The migration is one act, run after D2-D8 and D12 have landed and D9's fixture teeth are green. The charter's plan_fields is narrowed to exactly the census summary.plan (14 names) through the artifact door; then ticket_log.split runs over every ticket_file.plans(CairnCommons/tickets) path with actor 'cc' and why naming this ticket; then for every ticket reconstruct(plan, log lines the split added, state) is compared with the plan as it stood at HEAD (git show HEAD:<path>), and the run stops at the first mismatch, naming it. All of it, charter included, is one CairnCommons commit. A ticket the split cannot move is named and the commit is not made. Build order is not decision-number order: D12 landed in commit e81ee007, before the migration ran.

D12: cairn/machines/rehearsal/rehearsal.py reads the cursor with ticket_file.read_ticket (where it reads workflow_and_state for the FIXME cursor, it reads the merged doc) and keeps hashing the plan file's own bytes with design_sha, unchanged. Since the plan no longer carries workflow_and_state, berths, questions or any state key, a crossing or a berth write changes only the state file and a clean record stays matching. Tooth 6 of D9 measures it.

FIXME 1: add ticket_file.plans_of(id, tickets_dir) -> sorted [<id>.json, <id>-*.json] that are files and not .state.json; route the six remaining tickets-dir globs through it or plans(): a_failed_run_is_counted.py, cross.py, transitions.cast_ticket's held check, artifact.check_title and hollow._ticket_path take plans_of; cast.sweep_casts takes plans(tickets_dir) and its _is_ticket goes. The proof gains reader_plans_of_resolves_an_id_to_its_plans and the cast tooth calls sweep_casts over the fixture; criterion 4's grep then prints nothing.

Two existing files change, nothing new is made. (a) cairn/tools/chain/grammar.py, function ticket_path: the hex-id and slug lookups read a new module-level helper _ticket_plans(tickets_dir) that lists the dir once and indexes its <hex>-<slug>.json plans (never .state.json) by id and by slug, cached under the dir's os.stat st_mtime_ns and re-listed when that moves; the old per-call glob goes. (b) cairn/tools/determinism/determinism.py, function measure (it exists, line ~234, and holds the inner walk()): a dict shells_of local to measure caches shell_targets(root / path) per path, so each file is parsed once per report. Proof, all three files existing today: cairn/tools/base/proofs/test_base_probes_report_to_the_watch.py and cairn/tools/determinism/proofs/test_determinism.py, both green before the split, finish under the tester's 120 s budget again (measured 99 s and 50 s); cairn/tools/chain/proofs/test_chain_grammar.py stays green
